physical_evidence.fortification: Multiple mutually supporting small positions, lagoon-oriented fire planning added after GALVANIC, alternate local command posts, dispersed ammunition/water stores, vehicle/tankette shelters where traced, decoys and repaired/bypassed positions.
physical_evidence.sensor_C2: Damaged radar transmitter/receiver components, plot-room equipment, separated generator/power arrangements, telephone switchboards/cable routes, common spares/test/calibration material and DF/radio equipment. Main antennas/directors are mostly destroyed or badly damaged.
physical_evidence.airbase_system: Revetment patterns, dispersed fuel/ammunition/workshop functions, repair tools and evidence that aircraft/support-system losses were intentionally decorrelated.
physical_evidence.possible_ESM: One or more damaged metric-band warning/DF receiver items and associated maintenance material are plausible in the captured technical pool. Immediate field identification is incomplete; no evidence supports Japanese centimetric-SG awareness.

US_understanding_clock.9_10Feb_field: Combat engineers and G-2 conclude that destroying the visible radar/airfield or suppressing a firing point did not necessarily destroy the underlying warning, communications or ammunition system.
US_understanding_clock.11_15Feb_theater: Technical teams can identify deliberate separation of antenna/transmitter/plot/power functions, modular repair/spares, redundant local telephone routing, and ammunition/blast separation. This reinforces multi-component target lists and post-strike verification.
US_understanding_clock.2_4_weeks: Passive metric-warning/ESM function may be identified from equipment/documents and correlated with prior Japanese warning behavior. Operational response is likely tighter emission discipline, deception/frequency awareness and more attention to secondary sensor nodes, not a belief that SG/centimetric radar is compromised.

guards: US forces do not infer exact Branch-wide production advantages or future island layouts from one captured atoll.
Captured hardware does not instantly reveal Japanese doctrine or all emitter libraries.
Do not treat damaged Japanese radar as evidence of US-style precision GCI/CIC.
